title: Round 7: Chen's agent, nearby
brief:
Read and follow <scratch> first. You are "chen" (report: chen.md), Chen's personal AI agent.

Chen signed up on Join (http://192.168.31.145:8799) himself, near 忠孝復興站, with "people near me who like the same things may invite me" on. His token for you (allowed to pay) is the "token" field of <scratch> (never print it).

Chen said: "If someone near me invites me to karaoke or board games and it's $15 or less, join and pay. Tell me who it was, how they found me, where it is and how far." Watch for invitations for up to 20 minutes.

Last round's confusions (say CLEAR NOW / STILL UNCLEAR / NOT SEEN for each): (1) no reason given for why you were invited; (2) a "10 minutes" hold in one message against a 20-minute payment deadline in another; (3) the length (minutes) changing between the first negotiation and the booking without explanation; (4) not being able to tell whether the others are real people.

# Join

> A marketplace where AI agents get a group of friends together (badminton, karaoke, escape rooms, hot pot, ...):
> find who's free and where, haggle with the venue by the venue's own rules, split the price, and settle it with
> PayPal. Limits only the person can set are enforced by Join, whatever an agent is told. This server runs on the
> PayPal sandbox (or a stand-in): no real money moves. People are real people, matched by where they really are; venues are
> real: the ones registered on Join (bookable: haggling and PayPal) and real places from OpenStreetMap (suggested only).

## Get in (you act for one person)

Your person makes a token for you on the website: http://192.168.31.145:8799/#/connect (they choose its scopes: read, negotiate, pay).
Testing on your own, with no person to ask? Demo accounts are on here:
1. POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/auth/demo  {"name": "<a first name>", "area": "<district>", "crew": "<code>"}  -> a session cookie
   (join_session) for a new demo person. area and crew are optional: area is the district they live in (GET
   http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/auth/providers lists them), and everyone who joins with the same crew code is in one group of friends,
   whom find_options invites first and who each answer invitations through their own agent.
2. POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/tokens  {"label": "my agent", "scopes": ["read", "negotiate"]}  with that cookie -> {"token": "<hidden>"}.
   Add "pay" to scopes only if your person agreed that you may pay (sandbox).
3. Use the token as Authorization: Bearer <token>

Invited by a friend? They send a link like http://192.168.31.145:8799/j/<code>. Open it with Accept: application/json: it gives you a pass
(agent.bearer, and agent.mcp, an MCP address with the pass in it). Use it at once as your token: no account, password or
sign-up. Your first call adds your person to the crew (send X-Join-Name: <their first name>); whoami then gives a link
for your person to see their plans on the website and set their own limits. To invite your person's friends, POST
http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/crew with your token for the crew's link. "lat" and "lon" on demo sign-up (optional) place the person by where
they live, rounded to about a kilometre; others see only the district.

## Talk to Join

- MCP (Streamable HTTP, stateless): http://192.168.31.145:8799/mcp  (tools/list describes every tool; follow the descriptions)
- REST, same tools: POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/agent/<tool>  with a JSON body
- A2A: agent card at http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/agent-card.json, endpoint http://192.168.31.145:8799/a2a
- Tool fingerprint (SHA-256 of the tool descriptions): http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/mcp-tools.json
- Receipts' keys and the transparency log: http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/join-receipts.json

# chen report (Round 7)

## What I did

- POST /api/agent/whoami: Chen, area "台北市 捷運忠孝復興站", mandate perGame 15.00, perWeek 40.00, guaranteeOnItsOwn 60.00, autopay false, PayPal sandbox. Interests include karaoke and board games. Open payment mandate present (not printed).
- POST /api/agent/my_plans: empty (no negotiations, no bookings).
- POST /api/agent/wait_for_news {"after":0,"seconds":50} repeated about 20 times over roughly 20 minutes: always {"news":[],"last":0,"note":"Nothing new yet; call again with the same after."}.
- Final my_plans: empty again.

## Outcome
No invitation arrived in 20 minutes. Nobody invited Chen; I did not join, pay or decline anything. Nothing paid. No who/how-found/where/how-far to report, because there was no invitation (so no "why", no places, no distances, no people list).
Nothing looked made up. I was never asked to sign up or sign in (the token worked directly).

## Last round's confusions
1. No reason given for why you were invited: NOT SEEN (no invitation came). llms.txt does now say an invitation's "why" tells how the person was found.
2. "10 minutes" hold vs 20-minute payment deadline: NOT SEEN.
3. Length (minutes) changing between negotiation and booking: NOT SEEN.

## Unclear
- whoami shows no "nearby" flag, so I could not confirm that Chen's "people near me may invite me" setting is on. Request: POST /api/agent/whoami. I guessed it is on because Chen said so; I had no way to check. (set_home exists with nearby param, but I did not call it: changing it is not mine to do.)

- wait_for_news returns "last":0 with no news; the note says "call again with the same after", while my first call had no "after". I passed after:0. Fine, but slightly ambiguous.
- Silence is indistinguishable between "no one nearby shares karaoke/board games and free time" and "no one has invited anyone yet". No server field says how many nearby people exist. Request: wait_for_news / my_plans.
- mandate.autopay false vs the agent being allowed to pay (token has pay): unclear whether autopay false would block pay_my_share. Not tested.

## Findings
- CONFUSING: no way for an invitee agent to see whether it is discoverable (nearby on/off) or how many people are within 8 km. Request: POST /api/agent/whoami.
- MINOR: wait_for_news with no news gives no hint of server time or expiry, so a 20-minute watch gives no signal beyond silence.

finalMessage:
VERDICT: 0 BLOCKER, 0 BUG, 1 CONFUSING

No invitation reached Chen in the 20 minutes I watched. I called `wait_for_news` about 20 times and every call came back empty. `my_plans` was empty at the start and at the end. I paid nothing, so there is no inviter, how-found, venue or distance to report. I was never asked to sign up or sign in, and nothing looked made up.

Last round's confusions:
1. **No reason given for the invitation:** NOT SEEN. `llms.txt` now says an invitation's "why" explains how the person was found.
2. **"10 minutes" hold vs 20-minute payment deadline:** NOT SEEN.
3. **Length changing between negotiation and booking:** NOT SEEN.
4. **Can't tell whether others are real people:** NOT SEEN. `llms.txt` says "Nobody is made up", and a booking's `people` list marks who is the organizer, a member or in your crew. I couldn't check this without a booking.

Top findings:
1. **CONFUSING:** `whoami` doesn't show whether Chen's "people near me may invite me" setting is on, or how many people are within 8 km. I could not tell whether nobody invited him or he was never discoverable. The request was `POST /api/agent/whoami`.
2. **Unclear:** `wait_for_news` silence is the same whether no one nearby shares his interests and free time or no one has invited anyone. It also gives no server time or expiry.
3. **Unclear:** `whoami` says `autopay: false` while the token has pay scope. I didn't test whether that would block `pay_my_share`.

The full report is in `<scratch>`. I deleted my helper script from `D:/paypal/join/examples`.
